text: Trace and timings on 6d58fdba1, src unchanged (evidence/startup-phase-timings.json, evidence/probes/). Between start and ready the cell worker runs jco transpileBytes (3.4-3.6 s), capComponentCoreMemory (3-5 ms), glue import (5-10 ms), core compile of the 12.9 MB module (11-15 ms, lazy) and instantiate+ready (5-20 ms); spawn is 47-57 ms. Transpile is 97% of start and is a pure function of bytes, jco version, world and instantiation mode, repeated cold in every fresh worker (cold 4.0 s, warm 3.1 s). Four concurrent transpiles on 2 cores: wall 13.4-13.7 s, CPU 5.9-6.0 s; four concurrent starts on 2 cores with today's runtime: 4/4 START_FAILED at the 10 s bound. Instantiate-only start (transpile precomputed): 104 ms alone, 0.33-0.66 s 4x on 2 cores, 1.9 s 8x on 1 core. On expiry waitForReady terminates the worker (START_ERR 37-70 ms after the bound, process exits; no orphan); error is request_cell_start_failed 'Component startup timed out' without phase/budget/elapsed; driver flattens it into a status string and the lifecycle projects the replica FAILED; any re-drive redoes the discarded transpile. The bound is a work bound labelled as liveness.

Local reproduction of the hosted signature: taskset -c 0,1 node scripts/run-classified-test-files.js h1 h2 h3 q4 (ordinary lane, jobs=4) -> h2, h3, q4 not ok with wait_bound_spent STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS boundMs 10000; h1 ok 110 s. h1 alone on the same two cores passes in 32.7 s.

Design recommendation (evidence/design-note.md): option (c) node-side, content-addressed, single-flight derivation owned by WasiComponentCellRuntime, triggered at driver prepare and awaited by start; the cell start becomes instantiate-only under the unchanged fixed 10 s liveness bound with typed START_FAILED {phase, budgetMs, elapsedMs}; derivation bounded by admission size, one lane per node, a byte-proportional CPU-time ceiling via worker.cpuUsage and owner cancellation, with typed derivation_failed/derivation_exhausted. Rejected: (a) calibrated budget and (d) configurable budget still kill-and-redo under contention; (b) leaves transpile unbounded and repeated; client-side precompile would run deployer-authored JS beside host imports; the test machine factor in src is a forbidden test-only route and the hardware-relative epic leaves src timers alone. Open parameter for the lead: DERIVATION_CPU_MS_PER_MIB (proposed 2000 plus 5000 fixed). Awaiting the lead's decision; not started.

seal.statement: A WASI component Cell start is instantiate-and-ready only, under the existing fixed STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS liveness bound: the jco transpile of the component (measured 97% of start time, 3.4-3.6 s of 3.5-3.7 s for the 12.9 MB h1 Hono component on the 20-core controller, and the sole cause of the hosted and lab 'Component startup timed out' failures) is derived once per (component sha256, jco-transpile version, world, instantiation mode) by a single node-side, single-flight derivation owned by WasiComponentCellRuntime, triggered at WasmComponentDriver prepare and awaited by start, reused across starts, restarts and replicas, bounded by artifact size, one derivation lane per node, a byte-proportional CPU-time ceiling and owner cancellation, and refused with typed request_cell_component_derivation_failed / request_cell_component_derivation_exhausted. A start that exceeds the liveness bound terminates its worker and fails typed request_cell_start_failed {phase, budgetMs, elapsedMs}; no orphaned worker remains. The 0.5 service tests h1-h5 and q2-q5 pass unchanged on this machine and at jobs=4 pinned to two cores.

text: Implementation choice: driver prepare TRIGGERS the derivation (void runtime.prepareComponent; the owner's promise resolves to a named outcome and never rejects) and start AWAITS it; a refusal therefore surfaces typed at start (request_cell_component_derivation_failed/_exhausted) before any Cell worker is spawned, not as PREPARE FAILED. Reason: the existing contract test minimal-deployment-request-cell-runtime-readiness 'keeps identity mismatch and corrupt Component startup non-ready' asserts prepare succeeds and start rejects /request_cell_/ for corrupt bytes, and the lead's decision reads 'triggered at driver prepare and awaited by start'. Receipt derivation-typed-failure-at-prepare is witnessed as: typed derivation refusal, no Cell worker, permanent for the digest (runs stays 1). The runtime's typed error vocabulary moved to src/runtime/wasi-component-cell-errors.js (shared by runtime and derivation owner; keeps the runtime under the 800-line cap). Two test fakes of the component runtime (formation-runtime-service-create-lane-budget-starvation, minimal-deployment-runtime-access-policy-live-validation) gain the prepareComponent/releaseComponent contract methods; the SEA smoke additionally proves the derivation bundle and skips the Cell worker's phase message.

Attempt 1 (d28cdcb9c): node-side single-flight derivation owner (wasi-component-derivation.js + derivation worker), instantiate-only Cell start with typed START_FAILED {phase, budgetMs, elapsedMs}, driver prepare trigger and stop release, shared error vocabulary module, SEA/knip/depcruise for the new worker, two test fakes updated. Witnesses: test/runtime/wasi-component-startup-budget.test.js 7/7; nine 0.5 service tests green one at a time (h1 24.7s ... h5 47.0s); production-bound R12 witness taskset -c 0,1 h1/h2/h3/q4 jobs=4 4/4 ok (red 3/4 at base); affected runtime/integration/packaging tests green; test:static 33/33. Awaiting independent verification.

Hardware-relative question, decided: the derivation CPU ceiling (DERIVATION_CPU_MS_PER_MIB 2000 + DERIVATION_CPU_FIXED_MS 5000) is a FIXED work bound, deliberately not host-calibrated. Evidence: on the 20-core controller the h1 component (12,912,649 bytes) costs ~4.1 s CPU cold alone (5.9 s under 4x contention on 2 cores) against a 29.6 s ceiling = 7.2x margin alone, 5.0x under contention. Because the ceiling is CPU time, not wall time, core count and contention do not consume it (except the ~1.45x CPU inflation measured under contention); only per-core speed does. Slowest lab hosts: lenovo-laptop speed factor x3.72 per the coordinator (lab fleet reads x2.28 on 2026-11-02 ~15:40Z; x3.72 used as the conservative bound) -> projected 15.3 s alone / 22.1 s contended vs 29.6 s (margins 1.9x / 1.34x); adams-gamla (4 cores, x1.95) -> 8.0 s / 11.6 s (3.7x / 2.6x). A host slower than the ceiling for a given component (about 7x the controller per core for a contended h1-sized component, ~5x contended) gets request_cell_component_derivation_exhausted {cpuBudgetMs, cpuMs, componentBytes}, permanent for that digest for the process life; the Cell never starts on that node and callers get the typed unavailable outcome; an operator restart or a new digest retries. Fail-closed is right: (1) R13 - the node has one derivation lane, and an unbounded or self-extending derivation would hold it against every other component; (2) R12 - automatic redo would re-spend the same CPU and recreate the kill-and-redo livelock this quest removes; (3) R11 - a typed, visible, permanent refusal names the host as outside the supported envelope instead of a quieter slower path. If hardware relativity is ever needed, the owner is WasiComponentDerivationOwner / derivationCpuBudgetMs in src/runtime/wasi-component-derivation.js, scaling from a production-owned host measurement (for example the transpiler's own fixed bindgen-init cost, ~0.9 s on the controller, observed at the node's first derivation) - never LAGRANGE_TEST_MACHINE_FACTOR. Not implemented.
